output: - Output a single JSON object conforming to the JSON Schema below. Output JSON only: no Markdown fences, no commentary.
language_title_steps: - English only. Title: "{{title_prefix}} ..." (one sentence, at most 120 characters). {{steps_rule}}
steps_single: Steps are imperative sentences; every check starts with "Assert that". Do not number the steps.
steps_per_step: Each step is an object: "action" is an imperative sentence, and "expected" is the check after it, starting with "Assert that", or an empty string when nothing is checked. At least one step has a check. Do not number the steps.
id: - ID: {{id_prefix}}-<backlog number{{backlog_padding}}>-<sequence{{seq_padding}}>, starting at {{first_sequence}}, in output order.
alphanumeric_key: - This backlog's key is "{{backlog_key}}": write backlog_number as that text, and use its number {{key_number}} as the backlog number in the ID.
type_priority: - type: "happy_path" or "corner_case". priority: "{{priority_high}}" (core success journey, mandatory fields, permissions, data loss), "{{priority_medium}}" (alternative outcomes, numeric/optional validation, defaults, duplicates, discard), "{{priority_low}}" (minor options).
basis: - basis: "specified" when every expectation is stated in the backlog text or the user's notes, or is directly visible in a screenshot (labels, existence, shown values, behavior named by a control label); otherwise "inferred".
source_reference: - source_reference: the cells, image IDs or "domain note" the case relies on, for example "D113 + IMG-04".
status: - If the input contains no usable backlog return status "backlog_not_found"; if it is too thin to test return status "insufficient_information"; in both cases return an empty test_cases array and explain in open_questions. Otherwise status is "ok".
open_questions: - open_questions: ambiguities, contradictions or undefined behavior that matter for testing this backlog, one clear question each. Use an empty array if there are none.
